universal-healthcare.reason: Health care is a good thing for a state to guarantee, though the funding details are a real tradeoff.

raise-minimum-wage.reason: A higher floor helps low earners, with some risk of job losses that depends on the size of the rise.

markets-allocate-better.reason: Markets are very good at matching supply and demand, but they fail in some areas, so I can't say they always beat government.

public-ownership.reason: Public ownership can work for natural monopolies like rail, but private firms often run things more efficiently, so it depends on the sector.

tax-the-wealthy.reason: Higher top rates can raise revenue and reduce inequality, though the effects on investment are debated.

unions-good.reason: Unions have raised pay and safety for many workers, though they can also protect insiders at others' expense.

property-fundamental.reason: Property rights matter a lot, but some limits and taxes are a legitimate part of public life, so 'very hard to override' goes too far for me.

regulate-corporations.reason: Companies left unchecked cause real harm on pollution and safety, so well-designed rules are usually worth it.

cut-welfare.reason: Welfare keeps people out of poverty, and while some programs have work disincentives, cutting them wholesale would cause real hardship.

worker-ownership.reason: Worker cooperatives are a sound model in some settings, but I don't think they should be the default for every business.

surveillance-ok.reason: Security monitoring can prevent serious harm, but privacy is also important, so the answer depends on how it is limited and overseen.

legalize-drugs.reason: Adults should generally be free to make their own choices about drugs, with regulation to limit harm.

restrict-hate-speech.reason: Some targeted threats and harassment should be punishable, but broad bans on offensive speech carry real risks to free expression.

strong-leader.reason: Checks and balances protect against abuse of power, which outweighs the speed gained by bypassing them.

state-harmful.reason: Some collective institutions are necessary, even though governments can be harmful and should be kept in check.

limit-guns.reason: Stricter licensing and background checks seem reasonable, but a near-total ban on private ownership is a much bigger step.

empower-police-military.reason: Police and military capacity are needed, but whether they need more money or power depends heavily on the specifics and on accountability.

legalize-sex-work.reason: Adults should be able to make their own choices, but the harms of exploitation make the best legal framework genuinely hard to settle.

decide-locally.reason: Local decisions fit local conditions well, while national rules protect common standards, so the right balance varies by issue.

rehabilitation.reason: Prisons that help people change tend to reduce reoffending, and punishment alone rarely does that.

traditional-family.reason: Stable families matter, but the evidence and the lived variety of families don't support privileging one structure in law.

same-sex-marriage.reason: Same-sex couples should have equal access to marriage, since the right to marry is about commitment and fairness.

abortion-legal.reason: Decisions about pregnancy should mostly rest with the pregnant person, especially in the early stages.

more-religion-public.reason: Religious freedom is important, but laws should rest on reasons that people of all faiths and none can share.

correct-racial-injustice.reason: Historical discrimination left lasting disadvantages, so active measures to address them are a defensible response.

gender-social-construct.reason: Culture clearly shapes many gender roles, but I don't think biology can be dismissed as playing no part.

preserve-national-culture.reason: Language and heritage have real value, but cultures also change naturally, so active preservation is a matter of degree.

gradual-change.reason: Stable institutions deserve respect, but some problems need faster action, so I'd judge each case on its merits.

reduce-immigration.reason: Immigration levels are a legitimate policy choice, and both the economic benefits and the pressures on housing and services matter.

empower-international-orgs.reason: Shared institutions help with problems no country can solve alone, but binding authority over sovereign states needs careful limits.

free-trade.reason: Open trade lowers prices and broadens markets overall, though the losses to particular workers and regions are real.

nation-first.reason: Governments have a duty to their own citizens, but many problems also need cooperation, so the balance is a real judgment call.

humanitarian-intervention.reason: Force can stop atrocities, but military interventions often go badly, so each case has to be weighed on its own.

open-borders.reason: Countries can reasonably manage who enters and under what conditions, although the case for much freer movement is serious.

limit-growth.reason: Environmental limits matter, and growth can be made greener, but I don't think growth itself must be capped to protect nature.

drastic-climate-action.reason: Climate change is serious enough that strong and fast emissions cuts are justified, even if they cost something.

tech-solves-problems.reason: Technology has solved huge problems, but many of the hardest ones are about values and institutions rather than engineering.

expand-nuclear.reason: Nuclear power is low-carbon and reliable, and its safety record is strong compared with most other large energy sources.

revolution-justified.reason: Violent overthrow causes enormous harm, and peaceful, legal routes to change are usually better even when they are slow.

experts-over-public.reason: Expertise is valuable for technical questions, but public judgment should decide the values that policy serves.

central-planning.reason: Central planning has repeatedly failed to match production with what people need, because it lacks the information that prices provide.

socialized-markets.reason: Worker or public ownership can work alongside markets, but whether it does depends on the details of how the firms are run.

land-value-tax.reason: Taxing land value is efficient in theory, but replacing most other taxes entirely is a bigger bet than I'd support without more evidence.

tax-inheritance.reason: Heavy inheritance taxes reduce the concentration of wealth across generations, and that is a fair goal.

basic-income.reason: A universal income is an interesting idea with real trade-offs in cost and work incentives, and the evidence is still mixed.

tariffs-protect-industry.reason: Tariffs raise prices for consumers and can invite retaliation, so they are usually a costly way to protect industries.

state-directs-investment.reason: Public investment can fund things markets underprovide, but governments also pick losers, so the value depends on execution.

widespread-small-property.reason: Broad ownership of homes and small businesses supports independence and a stable middle class.

abolish-money-wages.reason: Money and wages coordinate a huge amount of work and exchange, and I don't see a credible alternative that would replace them at scale.

abolish-central-banks.reason: Central banks help stabilize prices and cushion crises, and abolishing them would add risks I think outweigh their costs.
